decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.aestronglyMeasurable_iInf_of_antitone
decls.doc:
`AEStronglyMeasurable` for the infimum of an antitone sequence of σ-algebras.

If `f` is `AEStronglyMeasurable` with respect to each σ-algebra in an antitone (decreasing)
sequence, then `f` is `AEStronglyMeasurable` with respect to their infimum.

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.aestronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto_ae'
decls.doc:
A.e. pointwise limit of `AEStronglyMeasurable[m]` functions is `AEStronglyMeasurable[m]`, for an
arbitrary measurable space `m` on `α` (no assumed relation to the measure's ambient σ-algebra `m₀`).
Mathlib's `aestronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto_ae` covers only the `m = m₀` case.

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.aestronglyMeasurable_iInf_of_tendsto_ae_antitone
decls.doc:
A.e. limit of an adapted antitone sequence is `⨅ n, 𝔽 n`-`AEStronglyMeasurable`.

For antitone `𝔽`, if each `g n` is `𝔽 n`-a.e.-strongly-measurable and `g n → Xlim` a.e., then `Xlim`
is `AEStronglyMeasurable[⨅ n, 𝔽 n]`. Codomain `β` at the same order level as the rest of this
section (`ℝ` qualifies).
decls.statement:
lemma aestronglyMeasurable_iInf_of_tendsto_ae_antitone
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}
    {𝔽 : ℕ → MeasurableSpace Ω} (h_antitone : Antitone 𝔽)
    {g : ℕ → Ω → β} {Xlim : Ω → β}
    (hg_meas : ∀ n, AEStronglyMeasurable[𝔽 n] (g n) μ)
    (h_tendsto : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => g n ω) atTop (𝓝 (Xlim ω))) :
    AEStronglyMeasurable[⨅ n, 𝔽 n] Xlim μ

decls.name: TauCeti.memLp_comp_of_bound
decls.doc:
A bounded measurable observable of an a.e.-measurable map belongs to every `Lᵖ` on a finite
measure space: if `f` is measurable, `g` is a.e. measurable, and `f ∘ g` is a.e. bounded, then
`fun ω => f (g ω)` is in `Lᵖ` for every exponent.

decls.name: TauCeti.Integrable.exp_norm_smul_of_ae_norm_le
decls.doc:
Multiplication by `exp (a * ‖x‖)` preserves integrability on a measure whose support is
essentially contained in a closed ball.
decls.statement:
theorem Integrable.exp_norm_smul_of_ae_norm_le (hg : Integrable g μ) (a R : ℝ)
    (hR : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ‖x‖ ≤ R) :
    Integrable (fun x : α => (Real.exp (a * ‖x‖) : 𝕜) • g x) μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Integrable.exp_abs_smul_of_ae_abs_le
decls.doc: Real-line version of `Integrable.exp_norm_smul_of_ae_norm_le`, stated with `|x|`.

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.condExp_indicator_eq_of_pair_law_eq
decls.doc:
If the pairs `(Y, Z)` and `(Y', Z)` have the same law, then for measurable `B` the conditional
expectations of `𝟙_B ∘ Y` and `𝟙_B ∘ Y'` given `σ(Z)` agree almost everywhere.
decls.statement:
theorem condExp_indicator_eq_of_pair_law_eq {Ω α β : Type*} [mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
    [MeasurableSpace α] [mβ : MeasurableSpace β] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (Y Y' : Ω → α) (Z : Ω → β) (hY : Measurable Y) (hY' : Measurable Y') (hZ : Measurable Z)
    (hpair : μ.map (fun ω => (Y ω, Z ω)) = μ.map (fun ω => (Y' ω, Z ω)))
    {B : Set α} (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
    μ[Set.indicator B (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) ∘ Y | MeasurableSpace.comap Z mβ]
      =ᵐ[μ] μ[Set.indicator B (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) ∘ Y' | MeasurableSpace.comap Z mβ]

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.condExp_ae_eq_of_forall_condExp_ae_eq_of_tendsto_eLpNorm
decls.doc:
**L¹-continuity of conditional expectation.** If `Xn → Xlim` in `L¹` (in `eLpNorm`) and each
`μ[Xn n | F]` agrees a.e. with a fixed `Y`, then `μ[Xlim | F]` agrees a.e. with `Y`.
decls.title: L¹-continuity of conditional expectation
decls.statement:
lemma condExp_ae_eq_of_forall_condExp_ae_eq_of_tendsto_eLpNorm
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}
    {F : MeasurableSpace Ω} {Xlim Y : Ω → ℝ} {Xn : ℕ → Ω → ℝ}
    (hXlimint : Integrable Xlim μ) (hXn_int : ∀ n, Integrable (Xn n) μ)
    (h_condExp : ∀ n, μ[Xn n | F] =ᵐ[μ] Y)
    (hL1 : Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (Xlim - Xn n) 1 μ) atTop (𝓝 0)) :
    μ[Xlim | F] =ᵐ[μ] Y

decls.name: TauCeti.lpBilinearForm
decls.doc:
The continuous bilinear form obtained by integrating an essentially bounded field of
continuous bilinear forms against two square-integrable functions.

decls.name: TauCeti.lpBilinearForm_apply
decls.doc: The `L∞`-coefficient bilinear form is the integral of its pointwise action.
decls.statement:
theorem lpBilinearForm_apply (μ : Measure X) (B : Lp (J →L[ℝ] J →L[ℝ] ℝ) ⊤ μ)
    (U V : Lp J 2 μ) :
    lpBilinearForm μ B U V = ∫ x, B x (U x) (V x) ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.lpBilinearForm_congr_ae
decls.doc:
Replacing an `L∞` coefficient field by an almost-everywhere equal field does not change
the associated bilinear form.

decls.name: TauCeti.integrable_bilinear_apply_of_memLp
decls.doc:
Applying an `L∞` field of bilinear forms to two `L²` functions gives an integrable
scalar-valued function.

decls.name: TauCeti.integrable_eval_of_forall_integrable_pow
decls.doc:
A real polynomial is integrable against any measure all of whose polynomial moments are finite.
The polynomial is a finite linear combination of the monomials `x ↦ xᵏ`, each integrable by
hypothesis.
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_eval_of_forall_integrable_pow
    (hmom : ∀ k : ℕ, Integrable (fun x : ℝ => x ^ k) μ) (q : ℝ[X]) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => q.eval x) μ

decls.name: TauCeti.memLp_two_eval_of_forall_integrable_pow
decls.doc:
A real polynomial is in `L²` against any measure all of whose polynomial moments are finite.
The square of a polynomial is again a polynomial, hence integrable by
`integrable_eval_of_forall_integrable_pow`, and `L²` membership is integrability of the square.
decls.statement:
theorem memLp_two_eval_of_forall_integrable_pow
    (hmom : ∀ k : ℕ, Integrable (fun x : ℝ => x ^ k) μ) (q : ℝ[X]) :
    MemLp (fun x : ℝ => q.eval x) 2 μ

decls.name: TauCeti.memLp_two_algebraMap_eval_of_forall_integrable_pow
decls.doc:
A real polynomial evaluation, cast into any `RCLike` scalar field, lies in `L²` against any
measure all of whose polynomial moments are finite.
decls.statement:
theorem memLp_two_algebraMap_eval_of_forall_integrable_pow {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜]
    (hmom : ∀ k : ℕ, Integrable (fun x : ℝ => x ^ k) μ) (q : ℝ[X]) :
    MemLp (fun x : ℝ => (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) (q.eval x)) 2 μ

decls.name: TauCeti.polynomialEvalLp
decls.doc:
Polynomial evaluation, cast into any `RCLike` scalar field, bundled as an `ℝ`-linear map into
`L²` against any measure all of whose polynomial moments are finite.
decls.statement:
def polynomialEvalLp (𝕜 : Type*) [RCLike 𝕜]
    (hmom : ∀ k : ℕ, Integrable (fun x : ℝ => x ^ k) μ) :
    ℝ[X] →ₗ[ℝ] Lp 𝕜 2 μ

decls.name: TauCeti.coeFn_polynomialEvalLp
decls.doc:
The `L²` representative of `polynomialEvalLp` is the expected scalar-cast pointwise
evaluation.
decls.statement:
lemma coeFn_polynomialEvalLp (𝕜 : Type*) [RCLike 𝕜]
    (hmom : ∀ k : ℕ, Integrable (fun x : ℝ => x ^ k) μ) (q : ℝ[X]) :
    ⇑(polynomialEvalLp 𝕜 hmom q) =ᵐ[μ] fun x : ℝ => (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) (q.eval x)

decls.name: TauCeti.eLpNorm_sqrt_smul_withDensity
decls.doc:
**Core seminorm identity.** The `L²(μ)` seminorm of `√w · g` equals the `L²(w·μ)` seminorm of
`g`, where `w·μ = μ.withDensity (ENNReal.ofReal ∘ w)`. Only nonnegativity of `w` almost everywhere
is needed.
decls.title: Core seminorm identity
decls.statement:
theorem eLpNorm_sqrt_smul_withDensity (hwm : AEMeasurable w μ)
    (hw_nonneg : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 ≤ w x) (g : α → 𝕜) :
    eLpNorm (fun x => Real.sqrt (w x) • g x) 2 μ
      = eLpNorm g 2 (μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (w x))

decls.name: TauCeti.withDensity_ac
decls.doc: `w · μ` is absolutely continuous with respect to `μ` (always holds).
decls.statement:
theorem withDensity_ac :
    (μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (w x)) ≪ μ

decls.name: TauCeti.ac_withDensity
decls.doc: `μ` is absolutely continuous with respect to `w · μ` (uses `w > 0` a.e.).
decls.statement:
theorem ac_withDensity (hwpos : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 < w x) (hwm : AEMeasurable w μ) :
    μ ≪ μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (w x)

decls.name: TauCeti.memLp_sqrt_smul
decls.doc: The forward direction `√w · f` of a class in `L²(w·μ)` is in `L²(μ)`.
decls.statement:
theorem memLp_sqrt_smul (hwpos : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 < w x) (hwm : AEMeasurable w μ)
    (f : Lp 𝕜 2 (μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (w x))) :
    MemLp (fun x => Real.sqrt (w x) • (f : α → 𝕜) x) 2 μ

decls.name: TauCeti.memLp_inv_sqrt_smul
decls.doc: The inverse direction `(√w)⁻¹ · g` of a class in `L²(μ)` is in `L²(w·μ)`.
decls.statement:
theorem memLp_inv_sqrt_smul (hwpos : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 < w x) (hwm : AEMeasurable w μ)
    (g : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) :
    MemLp (fun x => (Real.sqrt (w x))⁻¹ • (g : α → 𝕜) x) 2
      (μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (w x))

decls.name: TauCeti.weightL2Isometry
decls.doc:
**The weight ↔ measure isometry.** For an almost-everywhere-positive weight `w`, multiplication
by `√w` is a linear isometric equivalence `L²(w·μ) ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] L²(μ)`.
decls.title: The weight ↔ measure isometry
decls.statement:
def weightL2Isometry (hwpos : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 < w x) (hwm : AEMeasurable w μ) :
    Lp 𝕜 2 (μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (w x)) ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] Lp 𝕜 2 μ

decls.name: TauCeti.weightL2Isometry_apply
decls.doc: The forward isometry is multiplication by `√w`.
decls.statement:
theorem weightL2Isometry_apply (hwpos : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 < w x) (hwm : AEMeasurable w μ)
    (f : Lp 𝕜 2 (μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (w x))) :
    weightL2Isometry μ w hwpos hwm f =ᵐ[μ] fun x => Real.sqrt (w x) • (f : α → 𝕜) x

decls.name: TauCeti.weightL2Isometry_symm_apply
decls.doc: The inverse isometry is multiplication by `(√w)⁻¹`.
decls.statement:
theorem weightL2Isometry_symm_apply (hwpos : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 < w x) (hwm : AEMeasurable w μ)
    (g : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) :
    (weightL2Isometry μ w hwpos hwm).symm g
      =ᵐ[μ] fun x => (Real.sqrt (w x))⁻¹ • (g : α → 𝕜) x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_eq_zero_of_odd
decls.doc:
**An odd integrand integrates to zero over a symmetric interval.** No integrability
hypothesis is needed: the substitution `t ↦ -t` maps `[-R, R]` to itself, so the integral equals
its own negative.
decls.title: An odd integrand integrates to zero over a symmetric interval
decls.statement:
theorem integral_eq_zero_of_odd {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    {g : ℝ → E} (hodd : Function.Odd g) (R : ℝ) :
    ∫ t in (-R)..R, g t = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.setIntegral_eq_zero_of_isPiSystem
decls.doc:
**The Dynkin (π-λ) step for Bochner integrals.** A function whose integral vanishes on the
whole space and on every member of a generating π-system has vanishing integral on every
measurable set.
decls.title: The Dynkin (π-λ) step for Bochner integrals

decls.name: TauCeti.ae_of_ae_fst
decls.doc: An a.e. statement on the first factor transfers to the product measure.
decls.statement:
theorem ae_of_ae_fst {p : α → Prop} (hp : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, p x) :
    ∀ᵐ q : α × β ∂(μ.prod ν), p q.1

decls.name: TauCeti.ae_of_ae_snd
decls.doc: An a.e. statement on the second factor transfers to the product measure.
decls.statement:
theorem ae_of_ae_snd {p : β → Prop} (hp : ∀ᵐ y ∂ν, p y) :
    ∀ᵐ q : α × β ∂(μ.prod ν), p q.2

decls.name: TauCeti.setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_prod
decls.doc:
**The Dynkin (π-λ) step for Bochner integrals on a product space.** A function whose integral
vanishes on every measurable rectangle has vanishing integral on every measurable set.

This is `TauCeti.setIntegral_eq_zero_of_isPiSystem` at the π-system of measurable rectangles.
decls.title: The Dynkin (π-λ) step for Bochner integrals on a product space
decls.statement:
theorem setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_prod {ρ : Measure (α × β)} {f : α × β → E}
    (hf : Integrable f ρ)
    (hrect : ∀ s, MeasurableSet s → ∀ t, MeasurableSet t → ∫ p in s ×ˢ t, f p ∂ρ = 0) :
    ∀ u, MeasurableSet u → ∫ p in u, f p ∂ρ = 0

decls.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.measurable_coe_toMeasure
decls.doc:
Evaluation at a fixed measurable set is measurable on `FiniteMeasure α`. Private: it exists
only to prove the instance below.
decls.statement:
theorem FiniteMeasure.measurable_coe_toMeasure {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    Measurable fun ν : FiniteMeasure α => (ν : Measure α) s

decls.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.instMeasurableSingletonClass
decls.doc:
**Singletons are measurable in the space of finite measures**, when the σ-algebra on `α` is
countably generated.
decls.title: Singletons are measurable in the space of finite measures
decls.statement:
instance FiniteMeasure.instMeasurableSingletonClass [CountablyGenerated α] :
    MeasurableSingletonClass (FiniteMeasure α)

decls.name: MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.instMeasurableSingletonClass
decls.doc:
**Singletons are measurable in the space of probability measures**, when the σ-algebra on `α`
is countably generated. Pulled back from the finite-measure instance along the injective measurable
map `ProbabilityMeasure.toFiniteMeasure`, so the argument is not repeated.
decls.title: Singletons are measurable in the space of probability measures
decls.statement:
instance ProbabilityMeasure.instMeasurableSingletonClass [CountablyGenerated α] :
    MeasurableSingletonClass (ProbabilityMeasure α)

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.map_bind
decls.doc:
**Naturality of `bind`.** Pushing a `Measure.bind` mixture forward by a measurable map
commutes with the bind: the pushforward of the mixture is the mixture of the pushforwards, i.e.
the Giry-monad identity `map F ∘ bind g = bind (map F ∘ g)`.

Obtained from associativity of `bind` together with `bind_dirac_eq_map`.
decls.title: Naturality of `bind`
decls.statement:
theorem map_bind {μ : Measure S} {g : S → Measure γ} (hg : AEMeasurable g μ)
    {F : γ → δ} (hF : Measurable F) :
    (μ.bind g).map F = μ.bind fun ω => (g ω).map F

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.bind_map
decls.doc:
**Binding after a pushforward.** Binding `g` against a pushforward measure reindexes the
mixing measure: `bind g ∘ map f = bind (g ∘ f)`.

This is the `Measure` form of `PMF.bind_map`, and like it is a `simp` lemma: it rewrites a bind of
a mapped measure into the canonical single-bind form.
decls.title: Binding after a pushforward
decls.statement:
theorem bind_map {μ : Measure S} {f : S → γ} (hf : AEMeasurable f μ)
    {g : γ → Measure δ} (hg : AEMeasurable g (μ.map f)) :
    (μ.map f).bind g = μ.bind (g ∘ f)

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.lintegral_prod_eq_of_bind_eq
decls.doc:
Equal mixtures have equal rectangle probabilities, hence equal mixed moments of the evaluation
maps over an arbitrary finite family of measurable sets — repetitions allowed.
decls.statement:
theorem lintegral_prod_eq_of_bind_eq
    (h : (π₁.bind fun P => Measure.infinitePi fun _ : ℕ => (P : Measure α))
      = π₂.bind fun P => Measure.infinitePi fun _ : ℕ => (P : Measure α))
    {n : ℕ} (B : Fin n → Set α) (hB : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (B i)) :
    ∫⁻ P, ∏ i, (P : Measure α) (B i) ∂π₁ = ∫⁻ P, ∏ i, (P : Measure α) (B i) ∂π₂

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.lintegral_prod_pow_eq_of_bind_eq
decls.doc:
The monomial form. Since `lintegral_prod_eq_of_bind_eq` allows repetitions in the family,
listing `B j` exactly `m j` times turns the rectangle identity into one for the mixed monomial
`∏ j, (P (B j)) ^ m j`.
decls.statement:
theorem lintegral_prod_pow_eq_of_bind_eq
    (h : (π₁.bind fun P => Measure.infinitePi fun _ : ℕ => (P : Measure α))
      = π₂.bind fun P => Measure.infinitePi fun _ : ℕ => (P : Measure α))
    {k : ℕ} (B : Fin k → Set α) (hB : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (B i)) (m : Fin k → ℕ) :
    ∫⁻ P, ∏ j, ((P : Measure α) (B j)) ^ m j ∂π₁
      = ∫⁻ P, ∏ j, ((P : Measure α) (B j)) ^ m j ∂π₂

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.toReal_prod_pow
decls.doc:
The `ℝ≥0∞`-valued mixed monomial is `ENNReal.ofReal` of its real-valued counterpart; a
probability measure's values are finite, so `toReal` passes through the product.
decls.statement:
theorem toReal_prod_pow (P : ProbabilityMeasure α) {k : ℕ} (B : Fin k → Set α)
    (m : Fin k → ℕ) :
    (∏ j, ((P : Measure α) (B j)) ^ m j).toReal = ∏ j, (P (B j) : ℝ) ^ m j

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.bind_infinitePi_univ
decls.doc:
The mixture has the same total mass as the mixing measure, since every infinite product of
probability measures is itself a probability measure.
decls.statement:
theorem bind_infinitePi_univ (π : Measure (ProbabilityMeasure α)) :
    (π.bind fun P => Measure.infinitePi fun _ : ℕ => (P : Measure α)) Set.univ = π Set.univ

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.Measure.ext_of_bind_infinitePi_eq
decls.doc:
**The i.i.d. mixture determines the mixing measure.** If two finite measures on
`ProbabilityMeasure α` induce the same mixture `π.bind (P ↦ P^{⊗ℕ})`, they are equal.

The mixture's finite-dimensional rectangle probabilities are the mixed moments of the evaluation
maps, and repetitions in the rectangle turn those into mixed monomials. Each finite evaluation
family lands in the compact box `[0,1]^k`, so multivariate moment determinacy identifies its law,
and finite evaluation laws determine the measure.
decls.title: The i.i.d. mixture determines the mixing measure
decls.statement:
theorem Measure.ext_of_bind_infinitePi_eq [IsFiniteMeasure π₁]
    (h : (π₁.bind fun P => Measure.infinitePi fun _ : ℕ => (P : Measure α))
      = π₂.bind fun P => Measure.infinitePi fun _ : ℕ => (P : Measure α)) :
    π₁ = π₂

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.MeasIdx
decls.doc: The index type for the all-evaluations map: the measurable subsets of `α`.
decls.statement: abbrev MeasIdx (α : Type*) [MeasurableSpace α]

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.evalReal
decls.doc:
The all-evaluations map, sending a probability measure to its vector of real-valued
measures of the measurable sets.
decls.statement: def evalReal (P : ProbabilityMeasure α) : MeasIdx α → ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.measurable_probabilityMeasure_apply_real
decls.doc:
Evaluating a probability measure at a fixed measurable set is measurable, as a real-valued
function of the measure.
decls.statement:
theorem measurable_probabilityMeasure_apply_real {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    Measurable fun P : ProbabilityMeasure α => (P s : ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.measurable_probabilityMeasure_toMeasure_apply
decls.doc:
Evaluating a probability measure at a fixed measurable set is measurable, as an `ℝ≥0∞`-valued
function of the underlying measure.
decls.statement:
theorem measurable_probabilityMeasure_toMeasure_apply {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    Measurable fun P : ProbabilityMeasure α => (P : Measure α) s

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.measurable_probabilityMeasure_toMeasure_apply_toReal
decls.doc:
Evaluating a probability measure at a fixed measurable set is measurable, in the
`((P : Measure α) s).toReal` form.

Stated separately from `measurable_probabilityMeasure_apply_real` so that consumers whose goal is
phrased through `Measure.toReal` need not cross the coercion themselves.
decls.statement:
theorem measurable_probabilityMeasure_toMeasure_apply_toReal {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    Measurable fun P : ProbabilityMeasure α => ((P : Measure α) s).toReal

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.measurable_probabilityMeasure_eval_family
decls.doc: A family of evaluations is measurable into the product.

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.evalReal_apply
decls.doc:
The defining equation of `evalReal`, stated so that proofs about it cite the unfolding
explicitly rather than relying on definitional equality.
decls.statement:
theorem evalReal_apply (P : ProbabilityMeasure α) (s : MeasIdx α) :
    evalReal P s = (P s.1 : ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.measurable_evalReal
decls.statement: theorem measurable_evalReal : Measurable (evalReal (α := α))

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.measurableSpace_measure_eq_comap_eval
decls.doc:
The Giry σ-algebra on `Measure α` is the pullback of the product σ-algebra along the
all-evaluations map. This is a repackaging of the definition: the instance is already an `iSup`
of comaps of the individual evaluations.
decls.statement:
theorem measurableSpace_measure_eq_comap_eval :
    (Measure.instMeasurableSpace : MeasurableSpace (Measure α))
      = MeasurableSpace.comap (fun μ : Measure α => fun s : MeasIdx α => μ s.1)
          MeasurableSpace.pi

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.coe_apply_eq_ofReal_evalReal
decls.doc:
Expresses the `ℝ≥0∞`-valued evaluation `P ↦ (P : Measure α) s` as `ENNReal.ofReal` of its
real-valued counterpart `evalReal`.
decls.statement:
theorem coe_apply_eq_ofReal_evalReal (s : MeasIdx α) :
    (fun P : ProbabilityMeasure α => (P : Measure α) s.1)
      = fun P => ENNReal.ofReal (evalReal P s)

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.measurableSpace_probabilityMeasure_eq_comap
decls.doc:
The σ-algebra on `ProbabilityMeasure α` is the pullback of the product σ-algebra along
`evalReal`. The real-valued evaluations generate the same σ-algebra as the `ℝ≥0∞`-valued ones
defining the Giry structure, since each is measurable in terms of the other.
decls.statement:
theorem measurableSpace_probabilityMeasure_eq_comap :
    (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace (ProbabilityMeasure α))
      = MeasurableSpace.comap (evalReal (α := α)) MeasurableSpace.pi

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.Measure.ext_of_forall_map_probabilityMeasure_eval_eq
decls.doc:
**Finite evaluation laws determine the measure.** Two measures on `ProbabilityMeasure α` are
equal as soon as, for every finite family `B` of measurable subsets of `α`, the pushforwards under
the evaluation map `P ↦ (P (B 0), …, P (B (n-1)))` agree.

Only `π₁` need be assumed finite: the `n = 0` instance of the hypothesis equates the total
masses.
decls.title: Finite evaluation laws determine the measure
decls.statement:
theorem Measure.ext_of_forall_map_probabilityMeasure_eval_eq
    {π₁ π₂ : Measure (ProbabilityMeasure α)} [IsFiniteMeasure π₁]
    (h : ∀ (n : ℕ) (B : Fin n → Set α), (∀ i, MeasurableSet (B i)) →
      π₁.map (fun P => fun i => (P (B i) : ℝ))
        = π₂.map (fun P => fun i => (P (B i) : ℝ))) :
    π₁ = π₂

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.measurable_probabilityMeasure_pi
decls.doc:
The finite product combinator `ProbabilityMeasure.pi` is a measurable map
`(Π i, ProbabilityMeasure (α i)) → ProbabilityMeasure (Π i, α i)`.
decls.statement:
theorem measurable_probabilityMeasure_pi :
    Measurable (ProbabilityMeasure.pi : (∀ i, ProbabilityMeasure (α i)) → ProbabilityMeasure
      (∀ i, α i))

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.measurable_probabilityMeasure_pi_toMeasure
decls.doc:
A finite product of measurable probability-measure kernels is a measurable measure-valued map:
if each `ν i : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure (α i)` is measurable, then
`ω ↦ (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun i => ν i ω).toMeasure` is measurable.
decls.statement:
theorem measurable_probabilityMeasure_pi_toMeasure
    (ν : ∀ i, Ω → ProbabilityMeasure (α i)) (hν : ∀ i, Measurable (ν i)) :
    Measurable fun ω => (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun i => ν i ω).toMeasure

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_probabilityMeasure_pi_toMeasure
decls.doc:
A finite product of a.e.-measurable probability-measure kernels is an a.e.-measurable
measure-valued map: if each `ν i : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure (α i)` is `AEMeasurable`, then so is
`ω ↦ (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun i => ν i ω).toMeasure`.
decls.statement:
theorem aemeasurable_probabilityMeasure_pi_toMeasure
    (ν : ∀ i, Ω → ProbabilityMeasure (α i)) (hν : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (ν i) μ) :
    AEMeasurable (fun ω => (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun i => ν i ω).toMeasure) μ

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_probabilityMeasure_pi_toMeasure_of_measurable
decls.doc: Measurable-input corollary of `aemeasurable_probabilityMeasure_pi_toMeasure`.
decls.statement:
theorem aemeasurable_probabilityMeasure_pi_toMeasure_of_measurable
    (ν : ∀ i, Ω → ProbabilityMeasure (α i)) (hν : ∀ i, Measurable (ν i)) :
    AEMeasurable (fun ω => (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun i => ν i ω).toMeasure) μ

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.measurable_probabilityMeasure_pi_const_toMeasure
decls.doc:
Constant-coordinate specialization of `measurable_probabilityMeasure_pi_toMeasure`: the random
product `ω ↦ (ν ω)^{⊗ Fin m}` is measurable.

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_probabilityMeasure_pi_const_toMeasure
decls.doc:
Constant-coordinate specialization of `aemeasurable_probabilityMeasure_pi_toMeasure`: the random
product `ω ↦ (ν ω)^{⊗ Fin m}` is `AEMeasurable` from an a.e.-measurable kernel `ν`.

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.measurable_dirac_prod_probabilityMeasure_pi_const_toMeasure
decls.doc:
**Joint-kernel measurability.** The random measure
`ω ↦ δ_{ν ω} ⊗ (ν ω)^{⊗ Fin m}` on `ProbabilityMeasure α × (Fin m → α)` is measurable.

This is the joint-space companion of `measurable_probabilityMeasure_pi_const_toMeasure`: where that
one gives the block kernel alone, this one pairs it with a Dirac mass at the mixing measure itself,
which is what a conditional (joint-law) reading of the de Finetti mixture identity has to speak
about. It supplies the `Measure.bind_apply` and measure-extensionality inputs on the joint space
(`TauCetiRoadmap/Exchangeability/README.md`, Layer 1). No hypotheses beyond measurability of `ν`.
decls.title: Joint-kernel measurability
decls.statement:
theorem measurable_dirac_prod_probabilityMeasure_pi_const_toMeasure {α : Type*}
    [MeasurableSpace α] {m : ℕ} (ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α) (hν : Measurable ν) :
    Measurable fun ω =>
      (Measure.dirac (ν ω)).prod (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun _ : Fin m => ν ω).toMeasure

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.measurable_infinitePi
decls.doc:
**Product measurability in the measure argument.** For an arbitrary index type and a dependent
family of measurable spaces, `p ↦ ⊗ᵢ p i` is a measurable map
`(∀ i, ProbabilityMeasure (β i)) → Measure (∀ i, β i)`.

This is the arbitrary-index companion of `measurable_probabilityMeasure_pi_toMeasure`, which covers
the finite case through `ProbabilityMeasure.pi`. Mathlib supplies `Measure.infinitePi` and its
projective-limit API but not this measurability, which is what a mixture of such products needs for
`Measure.bind_apply` and for evaluating the mixture as an integral — the shape the de Finetti
mixture representation takes.
decls.title: Product measurability in the measure argument
decls.statement:
theorem measurable_infinitePi {ι' : Type*} {β : ι' → Type*} [∀ i, MeasurableSpace (β i)] :
    Measurable fun p : ∀ i, ProbabilityMeasure (β i) =>
      Measure.infinitePi fun i => (p i : Measure (β i))

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.measurable_infinitePi_const
decls.doc:
Constant-coordinate `ℕ` specialization of `measurable_infinitePi`: the countable power
`p ↦ p^{⊗ℕ}` is measurable.
decls.statement:
theorem measurable_infinitePi_const {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] :
    Measurable fun p : ProbabilityMeasure α =>
      Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ => (p : Measure α))

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.measurable_dirac_prod_infinitePi_const
decls.doc:
**Parameter-tagged product kernel.** For a measurable family of probability measures
`P : T → ProbabilityMeasure α`, the random measure `t ↦ δ_t ⊗ (P t)^{⊗ι}` on `T × (ι → α)` is
measurable, over an arbitrary index type `ι`.

This is the arbitrary-power companion of
`measurable_dirac_prod_probabilityMeasure_pi_const_toMeasure`, with the Dirac factor sitting on the
*parameter* rather than on the measure it selects. It is what a mixture that retains its parameter
as a coordinate needs for `Measure.bind_apply`.
decls.title: Parameter-tagged product kernel
decls.statement:
theorem measurable_dirac_prod_infinitePi_const {T α ι' : Type*} [MeasurableSpace T]
    [MeasurableSpace α] (P : T → ProbabilityMeasure α) (hP : Measurable P) :
    Measurable fun t =>
      (Measure.dirac t).prod (Measure.infinitePi fun _ : ι' => (P t : Measure α))

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.map_prefixProj_infinitePi
decls.doc:
**Finite-prefix marginal of a countable product.** Restricting `⊗ⱼ p j` to its first `n`
coordinates gives the finite product `⊗_{i : Fin n} p i`.

Mathlib's `Measure.infinitePi_map_restrict` gives the marginal along a `Finset.restrict`, indexed by
the coerced finite set; this is the `Fin n`-prefix form, which is what prefix-marginal arguments on
`ℕ → α` use. Stated with the bare prefix map rather than any particular prefix abbreviation, so it
stays independent of downstream conventions.
decls.title: Finite-prefix marginal of a countable product
decls.statement:
theorem map_prefixProj_infinitePi {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] (p : ℕ → ProbabilityMeasure α)
    (n : ℕ) :
    (Measure.infinitePi fun j : ℕ => (p j : Measure α)).map (fun x : ℕ → α => fun i : Fin n => x i)
      = Measure.pi fun i : Fin n => (p i : Measure α)

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.map_prefixProj_infinitePi_const
decls.doc:
Constant-coordinate specialization of `map_prefixProj_infinitePi`: the first `n` coordinates of
`p^{⊗ℕ}` are distributed as `p^{⊗ Fin n}`.
decls.statement:
theorem map_prefixProj_infinitePi_const {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] (p : ProbabilityMeasure α)
    (n : ℕ) :
    (Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ => (p : Measure α))).map (fun x : ℕ → α => fun i : Fin n => x i)
      = Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin n => (p : Measure α))

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.map_infinitePi_pair_block
decls.doc:
**Selecting a block from an i.i.d. power, tagged with its own law.** Reading an injective block
`k : Fin m → ℕ` of coordinates off the countable power `Q^{⊗ℕ}` and recording `Q` alongside the
result gives `δ_Q ⊗ Q^{⊗ Fin m}`; injectivity is what makes the selected coordinates independent.

This is `map_prefixProj_infinitePi_const` for an arbitrary injective block rather than a prefix,
paired with the law, which is the form a disintegration against a directing measure consumes.
decls.title: Selecting a block from an i.i.d. power, tagged with its own law
decls.statement:
theorem map_infinitePi_pair_block {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] (Q : ProbabilityMeasure α)
    {m : ℕ} {k : Fin m → ℕ} (hk : Function.Injective k) :
    (Measure.infinitePi fun _ : ℕ => (Q : Measure α)).map
        (fun x : ℕ → α => (Q, fun i : Fin m => x (k i)))
      = (Measure.dirac Q).prod (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun _ : Fin m => Q).toMeasure

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.bind_probabilityMeasure_pi_apply
decls.doc:
**Bind-evaluation.** Evaluating the mixture
`μ.bind fun ω => (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun i => ν i ω).toMeasure` on a measurable set `s` gives
`∫⁻ ω, … s ∂μ`, requiring only a.e.-measurability of each coordinate kernel `ν i`.
decls.title: Bind-evaluation
decls.statement:
theorem bind_probabilityMeasure_pi_apply
    (ν : ∀ i, Ω → ProbabilityMeasure (α i)) (hν : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (ν i) μ)
    {s : Set (∀ i, α i)} (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    (μ.bind fun ω => (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun i => ν i ω).toMeasure) s
      = ∫⁻ ω, (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun i => ν i ω).toMeasure s ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.bind_probabilityMeasure_pi_pi
decls.doc:
**Bind-evaluation on a rectangle.** On a rectangle `Set.univ.pi B`, the mixture equals
`∫⁻ ω, ∏ i, (ν i ω) (B i) ∂μ`.
decls.title: Bind-evaluation on a rectangle
decls.statement:
theorem bind_probabilityMeasure_pi_pi
    (ν : ∀ i, Ω → ProbabilityMeasure (α i)) (hν : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (ν i) μ)
    (B : ∀ i, Set (α i)) (hB : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (B i)) :
    (μ.bind fun ω => (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun i => ν i ω).toMeasure) (Set.univ.pi B)
      = ∫⁻ ω, ∏ i, (ν i ω : Measure (α i)) (B i) ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.bind_probabilityMeasure_pi_const_apply
decls.doc: Constant-coordinate `Fin m` specialization of `bind_probabilityMeasure_pi_apply`.
decls.statement:
theorem bind_probabilityMeasure_pi_const_apply {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] {m : ℕ}
    (ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α) (hν : AEMeasurable ν μ)
    {s : Set (Fin m → α)} (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    (μ.bind fun ω => (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun _ : Fin m => ν ω).toMeasure) s
      = ∫⁻ ω, (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun _ : Fin m => ν ω).toMeasure s ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.bind_probabilityMeasure_pi_const_pi
decls.doc:
Constant-coordinate `Fin m` specialization of `bind_probabilityMeasure_pi_pi`: the
finite-block mixture identity the de Finetti common ending consumes.
decls.statement:
theorem bind_probabilityMeasure_pi_const_pi {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] {m : ℕ}
    (ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α) (hν : AEMeasurable ν μ)
    (B : Fin m → Set α) (hB : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (B i)) :
    (μ.bind fun ω => (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun _ : Fin m => ν ω).toMeasure) (Set.univ.pi B)
      = ∫⁻ ω, ∏ i : Fin m, (ν ω : Measure α) (B i) ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.MeasureTheory.map_prefixProj_bind_infinitePi_pi
decls.doc:
The mixture's finite-dimensional rectangle probabilities are the mixed moments of the
evaluation maps: pushing `π.bind (P ↦ P^{⊗ℕ})` to its first `n` coordinates and evaluating on a
rectangle `∏ i, B i` gives `∫⁻ P, ∏ i, P (B i) ∂π`.
decls.statement:
theorem map_prefixProj_bind_infinitePi_pi {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α]
    (π : Measure (ProbabilityMeasure α)) {n : ℕ} (B : Fin n → Set α)
    (hB : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (B i)) :
    ((π.bind fun P => Measure.infinitePi fun _ : ℕ => (P : Measure α)).map
        (fun x : ℕ → α => fun i : Fin n => x i)) (Set.univ.pi B)
      = ∫⁻ P, ∏ i, (P : Measure α) (B i) ∂π

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_monotone_isCompact_measure_compl_le
decls.doc:
A tight family of measures admits a **monotone** exhaustion by compact sets whose complements
carry uniformly small mass: given tolerances `u j > 0`, there are compact `K j`, increasing in `j`,
with `σ n (K j)ᶜ ≤ u j` for every `n`. Accumulating the sets supplied by tightness is what turns
the unrelated compact sets into the monotone family Mathlib's Prokhorov criterion expects.
decls.statement:
lemma exists_monotone_isCompact_measure_compl_le
    {σ : ℕ → Measure α} (hTight : IsTightMeasureSet (Set.range σ))
    {u : ℕ → ℝ≥0} (hu_pos : ∀ j, 0 < u j) :
    ∃ K : ℕ → Set α, Monotone K ∧ (∀ j, IsCompact (K j)) ∧
      ∀ j n, (σ n) (K j)ᶜ ≤ (u j : ENNReal)

decls.name: TauCeti.finite_measure_cluster_limit
decls.doc:
A tight, uniformly mass-bounded sequence of finite measures has a weak cluster limit.

Given tightness of the sequence and a common total-mass bound, the conclusion is a finite limiting
measure with the same mass bound and weak convergence of all bounded-continuous test-function
integrals along an ultrafilter `U ≤ atTop`; no first-countability assumption on `FiniteMeasure α`
is needed.
decls.statement:
lemma finite_measure_cluster_limit
    (σ : ℕ → Measure α) (C : ℝ≥0)
    (hmass : ∀ n, (σ n) univ ≤ (C : ENNReal))
    (hTight : IsTightMeasureSet (Set.range σ)) :
    ∃ (μ₀ : Measure α) (U : Ultrafilter ℕ), (U : Filter ℕ) ≤ atTop ∧ IsFiniteMeasure μ₀ ∧
      μ₀ univ ≤ (C : ENNReal) ∧
      ∀ g : BoundedContinuousFunction α ℝ,
        Tendsto (fun n => ∫ x, g x ∂(σ n)) (U : Filter ℕ)
          (nhds (∫ x, g x ∂μ₀))

decls.name: TauCeti.finite_measure_subseq_limit
decls.doc: Sequential form of `finite_measure_cluster_limit` when `FiniteMeasure α` is first-countable.
decls.statement:
lemma finite_measure_subseq_limit
    [FirstCountableTopology (FiniteMeasure α)]
    (σ : ℕ → Measure α) (C : ℝ≥0)
    (hmass : ∀ n, (σ n) univ ≤ (C : ENNReal))
    (hTight : IsTightMeasureSet (Set.range σ)) :
    ∃ (μ₀ : Measure α) (φ : ℕ → ℕ), IsFiniteMeasure μ₀ ∧ StrictMono φ ∧
      μ₀ univ ≤ (C : ENNReal) ∧
      ∀ g : BoundedContinuousFunction α ℝ,
        Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x, g x ∂(σ (φ k))) atTop
          (nhds (∫ x, g x ∂μ₀))
